existence_argument.parameters: From hLip take L>0, K>=0, r>0. Let a=r/2 and r0=r/4. The real-valued function t -> norm(F(t,c)) is continuous on the compact interval [0,L], so choose C>=0 bounding it there. Set B=C+K*a and T=min(L,(a-r0)/(B+1)); then T>0 and B*T<=a-r0.
existence_argument.picard_hypotheses: The closed ball of radius a is inside the original open ball of radius r. The Lipschitz estimate gives norm(F(t,y))<=C+K*a=B on [0,T] times that closed ball. For fixed y, time continuity follows directly from hCont. These are precisely IsPicardLindelof with initial time 0, center c, domain radius a, initial radius r0, norm bound B and Lipschitz constant K. Finite-dimensional real normed spaces are complete. Apply IsPicardLindelof.exists_forall_mem_closedBall_eq_forall_mem_Icc_hasDerivWithinAt to obtain exactly the stated flow. Compactness and smoothness of M are not needed in this derivation once F and these hypotheses are available.

scope_reconciliation.general_local_field: For a source-admissible f on an open subset of R times R^n and an initial point (t0,x0), choose nested compact time-state cylinders inside that open set. Choose a continuous (or smooth) cutoff equal to 1 on the smaller cylinder with compact support in the larger one. Multiplying f by it and extending by zero gives a globally continuous field g(t,y) with compact support, agreeing with f(t0+t,y) near (0,x0). Uniform spatial Lipschitz regularity on a still smaller cylinder is inherited from f because the cutoff is identically 1 there.
scope_reconciliation.compact_realization: For n>=1 use S^n with a stereographic chart chi:S^n minus {p}->R^n, choose alpha=chi.symm(x0), and select chartAt alpha=chi. Define the raw E-valued tangent representative X(t,q)=g(t,chi(q)) for q != p and X(t,p)=0. Compact spatial support makes this jointly continuous at p as well as elsewhere. With I the identity model, the fixed-chart field in the root is exactly g. All compact, Hausdorff, sigma-compact and boundaryless manifold assumptions hold. The zero-dimensional case is trivial. Thus every source-admissible finite-dimensional local field can be represented, even though an arbitrary global Euclidean field need not admit this global compact presentation.
scope_reconciliation.time_and_domain: The root yields a forward solution from x0. Its continuity at zero allows shrinking the interval so that it stays where the cutoff equals 1 and therefore solves the original equation. Applying the same construction to -f(t0-t,y) yields a backward solution. Glue at t0: the two one-sided derivatives both equal f(t0,x0), giving the derivative there. Continuity of f then makes the derivative continuous locally. No uniqueness premise is needed for this existence-only gluing. Teschl Theorem 2.2 also explicitly states a forward-interval existence component.
scope_reconciliation.before_counterexample: For the raw field X=1 in the before counterexample, the after field is F=1 and flow(y,t)=y+t satisfies the revised equation. Pulling this curve back does not in general give an intrinsic integral curve of X, but the selected informal target is expressly Euclidean and the after conclusion does not assert that intrinsic property.
